dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.title: Law No. (3) of 2026 Concerning the Quality and Safety of Buildings
dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.snippet: Official text. Owners must obtain a building quality and safety certificate once a building is 20 years past its completion certificate, based on a technical report by a registered engineering office. Valid 10 years, or 5 years where the building is 40 or more years old.

dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.title: Mohammed bin Rashid issues law on quality and safety of buildings in Dubai
dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.snippet: Dubai Media Office announces the new law regulating the quality and safety of buildings across the emirate, including periodic certification of older buildings.

dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.title: Dubai Municipality sets 10-year and 5-year validity for building quality and safety certificates
dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.snippet: A municipality circular says owners of buildings completed 20 or more years ago must obtain the certificate; 10-year validity for buildings aged 20 to under 40, 5 years for 40 and over. Notices go out in stages, starting with multi-storey buildings over 40 years old.

dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.title: Dubai Municipality sets validity rules for building safety certificates
dubai.old_buildings.safety_certificate_r.snippet: Summary of the October 2026 circular: certificate required for buildings 20+ years old, renewal in the final 90 days before expiry, submissions through the Dubai Building Platform.

dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.title: Law No. (3) of 2026, Article 16
dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.snippet: Besides fines of AED 100 to AED 1 million, the municipality may, with Dubai Land Department, suspend or reject applications related to a non-compliant building, including lease contract attestation.

dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.title: Dubai issues law to boost building safety with fines of up to Dh2 million
dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.snippet: News report on the new building safety law: fines up to Dh1 million, doubled to Dh2 million for repeat violations, plus other measures against owners who do not comply.

dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.title: Dubai Law No. 3 compliance
dubai.ejari.attestation_needs_building_c.snippet: Engineering firm page warning owners that non-compliance can lead to Ejari suspension, DLD transaction freezes and permit halts.
